task.instruction: Find a report on the BBC News website about recent developments in renewable energy technologies in the UK.

final_answer:
I found a BBC News report on recent UK renewable energy developments: **"Bringing landfill into the 21st Century with solar power"** (published 5 days ago, by Alex Pope). Link: https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c6vg9vkd50vno

**Summary:**
- Infinis is building a solar farm on the Brogborough landfill site in Bedfordshire. It describes the site as "Europe's biggest landfill".
- The site covers 168 acres and will have more than 62,000 panels. They will produce about 40MWp, enough to power Cranfield University, or about 10,500 homes. Switch-on is planned for spring 2027.
- The site already turns methane from decomposing waste into 9MW of power for the national grid. The solar farm adds a second renewable source on the same land. Battery storage has planning permission too.
- Backers say that brownfield sites like this are a better option than farmland, which is a divisive issue. A sustainability lecturer at The Open University agrees that capped landfills suit solar. She notes that panels can change soil moisture and airflow.
- Infinis also plans a solar farm at its nearby Stewartby landfill site.

The search also turned up other recent BBC items on UK renewables:
- "'It's offensively cheap': How solar power is quietly becoming bigger than nuclear"
- "Turning the tides: Could hidden sea power energise our coastal towns?", about a tidal energy generator
- Wind farm and solar farm planning disputes, including the Dales wind farm and a West Oxfordshire solar plan

judge.rationale: Agent found and summarized a BBC News article, “Bringing landfill into the 21st Century with solar power,” about a UK solar/landfill energy project published 5 days ago.

final_page.title: Powering the future from Brogborough landfill site
